sources.title: IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report (2023)
sources.excerpt: Human activities, principally through emissions of greenhouse gases, have unequivocally caused global warming.
sources.note: Short educational excerpt; consult the original report for context.

sources.title: NASA Climate: Evidence
sources.excerpt: Multiple independent observations, including temperature measurements and satellite records, provide evidence of a changing climate.
sources.note: Educational paraphrase, not a verbatim NASA quotation.

sources.title: UNESCO Education for Sustainable Development
sources.excerpt: Education can help learners acquire knowledge, skills and values to make informed decisions and act responsibly.
sources.note: Educational paraphrase, not a verbatim UNESCO quotation.

lessons.title: Weather vs. Climate
lessons.concept: Weather describes short-term conditions; climate describes patterns over longer periods.
lessons.analogy: Weather is today's outfit; climate is the wardrobe you usually need.
lessons.example: A cold day does not, by itself, overturn a long-term warming trend.

questions.question: Which statement describes climate?
questions.feedback: Climate concerns longer-term patterns, not a single day's conditions.

questions.question: Does one cold day disprove long-term global warming?
questions.feedback: A single observation cannot establish or overturn a long-term trend.

lessons.title: Greenhouse Gases
lessons.concept: Greenhouse gases influence Earth's energy balance; human activities have increased their concentrations.
lessons.analogy: A blanket changes how quickly heat escapes; the analogy is imperfect but helps introduce the idea.
lessons.example: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which activity can increase atmospheric CO₂?
questions.feedback: Combustion of fossil fuels releases CO₂.

questions.question: What does the IPCC attribute modern global warming primarily to?
questions.feedback: The IPCC identifies human greenhouse gas emissions as the primary driver.

lessons.title: Mitigation and Adaptation
lessons.concept: Mitigation reduces greenhouse gas emissions or increases removals. Adaptation reduces risks from climate impacts.
lessons.analogy: Mitigation helps reduce the cause; adaptation helps prepare for consequences.
lessons.example: Cleaner electricity is mitigation; preparing drainage for intense rainfall is adaptation.

questions.question: Improving drainage for extreme rainfall is primarily...
questions.feedback: Drainage improvements can help communities adapt to flood risks.

questions.question: Replacing fossil-fuel electricity with low-carbon generation is primarily...
questions.feedback: This action can reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

lessons.title: Climate Information Literacy
lessons.concept: Reliable climate learning requires checking sources, dates, methods, uncertainty and whether a claim matches the cited evidence.
lessons.analogy: A citation is a map reference: you still need to check whether it leads to the right place.
lessons.example: Check whether a chart shows global long-term data or a single local year before drawing conclusions.

questions.question: A claim includes a URL. What should you do next?
options: Check whether the source actually supports the claim
questions.answer: Check whether the source actually supports the claim
questions.feedback: A URL alone does not prove that the claim is supported.

questions.question: Which is a warning sign?
questions.feedback: Unverifiable figures should be treated cautiously.

actions.title: Reduce avoidable food waste
actions.description: Plan meals and use stored food safely.

actions.title: Explore walking or public transit
actions.description: Consider accessible low-emission travel options where practical.

actions.title: Save electricity responsibly
actions.description: Switch off unnecessary lighting and equipment.

actions.title: Map local flood preparedness
actions.description: Identify safe routes and trusted local preparedness information.

actions.title: Check climate claims before sharing
actions.description: Verify source, date, context and uncertainty.
